To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a dual convolutional neural networks (CNNs) approach which uses transfer learning and achieves significant classification accuracy on a subset of PhysioNet Challenge Dataset.

our novel transfer learning approach can effectively screen for pre existing heart disease using simultaneously acquired ECG and PCG waveforms, while being robust to the limited amounts of data available.

we introduce a novel approach for the classification of heart diseases using transfer learning and we show that the transferable features from ECG and PCG can be used to classify heart diseases using synchronized PCG and ECg signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of screening heart diseases using a novel transfer learning based approach which is evaluated on the PhysioNet challenge dataset.
the problem of using transfer learning to effectively screen pre existing heart diseases using simultaneous ECG and PCG signals and our results show that our proposed approach can achieve this goal.
the development of novel methods for the analysis of PCG and EGC signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to achieve state-of-the-art results on a challenging problem of simultaneously classifying ECG and PCG waveforms.
our novel transfer learning based approach is able to effectively use the limited amount of available simultaneous PCG and EC G data to achieve significant performance.
the transfer learning approach is effective in the case of limited simultaneous ECG and PCG data, while having the capability of adapting to larger datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our novel transfer learning approach is able to provide a promising way for screening pre existing heart diseases using limited simultaneous ECG and PCG waveforms.
our method can effectively utilize limited number of synchronized ECG and PCG waveforms to screen for pre existing heart disease.
our method is able to achieve a classification accuracy of 0.83 on record wise evaluation framework and 0.84 on sample wise evaluation framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that

using a limited number of simultaneously collected ECG and PCG waveforms can lead to better screening performance than using individually collected ECG and/or PCG waveforms, and the transferable features from the individually collected ECG/PCG can help improve the classification performance.
using a limited amount of synchronized PCG-ECG data can lead to a better performance when transfer learning is used.

the transfer learning based dual convolutional neural networks can be effectively utilized to screen pre existing heart diseases using simultaneously acquired PCG or ECG signals, even with a limited number of training samples.
